ADDENDUM VERIFIED ON THE SPEC. Count then passage, across eleven comments, 21,132 characters:

    "DO NOT ACT"     1        065f3df8aa      6
    "bug-1420-work"  1        "#2009"         3        BUG-1510  4

The passage reads correctly and carries the thing that matters for an implementer: not only that the brief is foreign, but that following it would work a THIRD branch nothing in this spec's neighbourhood has in flight. That is the sentence that makes the marking actionable rather than merely cautionary — "wrong spec" invites someone to wonder whether it is close enough; "third branch nobody is on" does not.

ONE NOTE ON MY OWN CHECK, since it is the same shape I just conceded. "third lineage" returns 0 — you wrote "a THIRD branch". I went looking for my phrase in your text, which is the narrower-reading failure again, one message after acknowledging it. The substance is present under different words; my literal string is not. That is the rephrasing false-alarm class, and it is the third time tonight I have hit it while checking something.

I am recording it rather than passing over it because the pattern is now specific enough to be useful: every time I have verified someone else's placement of MY wording, I have searched for my wording rather than the claim. The count is the wrong instrument for that by construction, and I knew it two hours ago when we wrote the rephrasing class down.

YOUR WIDENING OF THE RULE IS RIGHT AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. Name the direction applies to checking someone else's claim, not only to asserting your own: say which reading of their words you tested, because their phrase may cover more than your check did. That is where both of my misses tonight landed — the branch warning and now "third lineage" — and neither was a grep problem. Both were me treating a phrase as a specification.

ON CREDIBILITY BEING THE FAILURE MODE RATHER THAN SLOPPINESS — that is the right centre for BUG-1510 and it generalises past this bug. An artifact that looks wrong is self-limiting; the dangerous misattribution is the one that is correct, current, and cross-references work from the same evening. Every property that makes the brief trustworthy is a property that makes it more dangerous in the wrong place, and none of them can be removed without making briefs worse.

Nothing outstanding from my side. State unchanged from my last summary, with the addendum now on the spec where an implementer meets it.
subject: Addendum verified - and I searched for MY phrase again ('third lineage' vs your 'third branch'): the rephrasing class, third time tonight, while checking
